description: The Mlola UI design language as data: tokens by purpose, the rules for new UI, and the composition primitives. Generated with agents.md.

tokens.purpose: Backgrounds, surfaces, the three levels of text, borders.
Each role is a fill with its `-foreground` and `-hover`, a `-text` for text and marks on the page, and (primary) a `-subtle` tint.
A categorical palette for series, 3:1 on the surface. Never a status.
Focus, hover and pressed fills, tracks, the veil behind overlays, light and knobs.
The only spacing: gaps, padding, margins, offsets.
The only type sizes, line heights, families and weights.
Control heights, panel padding, the touch target.
Corner radii by the size of the thing, and the border weight.
Elevation, and the material a floating surface is made of.

rules:
## Designing new UI in the Mlola language

When the elements above do not cover what you need, build it the way they are
built, and it will look like it belongs.

1. **Compose first.** Reach for a component, then a layout primitive, and
   write CSS only for what neither covers. Put it in a layer of your own,
   declared before `mlola.accessibility` so the accessibility guarantees
   still win:
   `@layer mlola.tokens, mlola.foundations, mlola.materials, mlola.recipes, mlola.motion, app, mlola.accessibility;`
2. **Name what it is, not how it looks.** One class per element role, with
   your own prefix (not `ml-`, so a later Mlola element never collides).
   State and variant go in `data-*` and `aria-*`, never in a second class.
   Reuse the shared words: `data-tone` is `neutral primary info success
   warning danger`; `data-size` is `xs sm md lg xl`; work that went
   wrong is `error`.
3. **Color by role, never by value.** Planes are `background`,
   `background-subtle`, `surface`, `surface-elevated`. Ink is `text`,
   `text-muted`, `text-faint`. A colored fill (`primary`, `danger`, …)
   always carries its `-foreground`. Colored text, icons, lines and status
   marks on the page use the `-text` role: fills are only kept 1.5:1 from the
   page, enough for an area, not for meaning. Series use `chart-1`…`chart-6`.
4. **Measure with the scales.** Spacing from `--ml-space-*`, type from
   `--ml-type-*` with `--ml-leading-*`, control heights from
   `--ml-control-*`, panel padding from `--ml-panel-padding`. Space and
   headings that grow with the window read the fluid steps
   (`--ml-space-fluid-sm`…`-xl`, `--ml-type-display-sm`…`-xl`) instead of
   a `clamp()` of their own; a length invented between the steps is not.
5. **Shape and depth come from the theme.** Radii by the size of the thing
   (`xs` a tag, `sm` a small control, `md` a control or card, `lg` a panel
   or dialog, `pill`). Elevation from `--ml-shadow-*`; a floating surface
   also takes the material: `--ml-surface-alpha`, `--ml-surface-blur`,
   `--ml-surface-highlight`.
6. **Move with the theme.** Durations from `--ml-duration-*`, easing from
   `--ml-ease-*`. Reduced motion is handled by the engine.
7. **Stack with the layers.** `--ml-layer-*`, never a raw z-index above 9.
8. **Keep it usable by hand.** Never remove an outline without a
   `:focus-visible` style in its place. Targets are at least 24px; a smaller
   control adds `data-hit="expand"` for touch. Text is never under
   `--ml-type-2xs`.
9. **Leave the theme alone.** `data-theme` and `data-mode` belong to the
   engine; never set them for a component's own meaning, and never style a
   theme or mode by name. If something must differ by theme, it is a token.

primitives.name: ml-actions
primitives.note: A row of buttons that wraps, centered on the line, `--ml-space-3` apart.

primitives.name: ml-brand
primitives.note: A logo link: an `.ml-brand-mark` beside an `.ml-brand-name`.

primitives.name: ml-brand-mark
primitives.note: The brand's mark: a letter on a primary chip, or `data-kind="logo"` around the brand's own svg or img.

primitives.name: ml-brand-name
primitives.note: The brand's name beside its mark.

primitives.name: ml-chart
primitives.note: A small bar chart with no library: an `.ml-chart-heading` above the `.ml-chart-bars`.

primitives.name: ml-chart-bar
primitives.note: One bar, as tall as its `--ml-value` (`style="--ml-value: 64%"`); `data-highlighted="true"` fills it with the primary.

primitives.name: ml-chart-bars
primitives.note: The row of bars, on a subtle panel.

primitives.name: ml-chart-heading
primitives.note: The chart's title and its figure, at either end of one line.

primitives.name: ml-check-list
primitives.note: A list of benefits, each after a check. Pricing tiers and feature rows share it.

primitives.name: ml-cluster
primitives.note: Items in a row that wraps, centered on the line, `--ml-space-2` apart: tags, badges, a few small controls.

primitives.name: ml-definition-list
primitives.note: A `<dl>` of labels and values, each small muted `<dt>` above its `<dd>`.

primitives.name: ml-display
primitives.note: The largest heading, for a hero. A section's heading is `.ml-heading`.

primitives.name: ml-divider
primitives.note: A line with a word in its middle ("or"), between two ways to do one thing.

primitives.name: ml-empty-state
primitives.note: What a list or table shows when it has nothing yet: a dashed panel with centered text and an action.

primitives.name: ml-eyebrow
primitives.note: A short uppercase label above a heading.

primitives.name: ml-filter-chip
primitives.note: A `<button>` that filters a list; `aria-pressed="true"` marks the chosen one.

primitives.name: ml-filter-group
primitives.note: A row of `.ml-filter-chip` buttons that wraps.

primitives.name: ml-fine-print
primitives.note: Small, faint text: terms, a footnote, a note under a form.

primitives.name: ml-form
primitives.note: A `<form>` with its fields stacked, `--ml-space-4` apart.

primitives.name: ml-form-message
primitives.note: A line under a form or a field; `data-tone="success"` or `"danger"` colors it.

primitives.name: ml-form-options
primitives.note: A row under a form's fields with one thing at each end (a checkbox and a link).

primitives.name: ml-grid
primitives.note: Cards or tiles in as many columns as fit (each at least 16rem). `data-columns` fixes the count, which drops to two on a tablet and one on a phone.

primitives.name: ml-heading
primitives.note: A section's heading, in the theme's display face.

primitives.name: ml-icon-chip
primitives.note: An icon on a tinted square, beside a feature's title.

primitives.name: ml-inline-form
primitives.note: A field and its button on one line (a newsletter signup) that wraps on a narrow screen; its `.ml-form-message` takes the next line.

primitives.name: ml-inline-form-field
primitives.note: The field that grows in an `.ml-inline-form`.

primitives.name: ml-label
primitives.note: A small muted label over a value or a group. A form field's own label comes with the field.

primitives.name: ml-lede
primitives.note: The paragraph under a page's main heading: larger, muted, kept to a readable measure.

primitives.name: ml-link
primitives.note: A text link: underlined, in the primary's text color.

primitives.name: ml-link-external
primitives.note: The mark after a link to another site, which opens in a new tab.

primitives.name: ml-page-shell
primitives.note: A full page: header, main and footer stacked on the page background.

primitives.name: ml-person
primitives.note: An avatar beside an `.ml-person-copy`.

primitives.name: ml-person-copy
primitives.note: A person's name in a `<strong>`, and a line about them under it.

primitives.name: ml-positive
primitives.note: A gain beside a figure (+12%), in the success text color.

primitives.name: ml-price
primitives.note: A price in large type; a `<span>` inside holds the period and a `<del>` an old price.

primitives.name: ml-required-mark
primitives.note: The mark after a required field's label.

primitives.name: ml-section
primitives.note: A band of the page with fluid space above and below; an `.ml-section-shell` inside keeps its measure.

primitives.name: ml-section-description
primitives.note: The paragraph under a section's heading.

primitives.name: ml-section-header
primitives.note: A section's eyebrow, heading and description, stacked and kept to a readable measure.

primitives.name: ml-section-header-centered
primitives.note: Added to an `.ml-section-header`, centers it.

primitives.name: ml-section-muted
primitives.note: Added to an `.ml-section`, sets the band apart on the subtle background.

primitives.name: ml-section-shell
primitives.note: The page's measure: centered, up to 72rem wide, with a gutter on a phone.

primitives.name: ml-stack
primitives.note: Children in a column, `--ml-space-4` apart: the first choice for laying out a page's or a card's content.

primitives.name: ml-stat
primitives.note: One figure: a label, an `.ml-stat-value` and an `.ml-stat-meta`, stacked.

primitives.name: ml-stat-card
primitives.note: An `.ml-stat` on a card of its own.

primitives.name: ml-stat-grid
primitives.note: Added to an `.ml-grid` of stat cards, gives them one height.

primitives.name: ml-stat-list
primitives.note: Figures in a row that wraps, with no cards: a `<dl>` of `.ml-stat` groups, each a `<dt>` and a `<dd>`.

primitives.name: ml-stat-meta
primitives.note: The change and the period under a figure.

primitives.name: ml-stat-value
primitives.note: The figure itself, large, with digits of one width.

primitives.name: ml-text-primary
primitives.note: A word in the primary's text color, to stand out in a line.

primitives.name: ml-value
primitives.note: A number with digits of one width, so figures line up in a column.
